title: Sales snackpack: 5-slide speed & value scripts (iter2)
content:
Purpose
One-page speaker notes + five micro-slides to help AEs/SDRs run 3–8 minute calls focused on speed-to-value and clear deployment pathways. This is meant to be a compact, portable kit for late-discovery conversations where customers care about latency, cost, and predictable production paths.

How to use (TL;DR)
- 0–30s: Set context with persona hook (platform engineer/product/CTO)
- 30–90s: Deliver the 90-second value pitch (problem, Redwood approach, proof)
- 90–180s: Micro-demo talking points or rapid architecture sketch
- 180–300s: Objection handling + next-step play (trial, architecture session, pricing intro)

Slide 1 — One-line opener + persona hooks
Title: "Why latency and cost are your product levers right now"
Speaker notes: Open with an empathy statement geared to the persona. For platform teams: "We hear teams hit unpredictable tail latency when traffic spikes and waste money on overprovisioning. Redwood gives you stable p50/p95 through smart routing and caching so you can make SLOs predictable." For product managers: "Slower responses kill engagement; we help you hit your latency SLO without blowing the budget."
Quick snippets to memorize:
- Platform engineer: "Predictable throughput, GPU pooling, and fallbacks so your service never trips."
- PM/CTO: "Deliver lower latency and lower per-token spend by letting us handle batching, KV caching, and model routing."

Slide 2 — 90-second value pitch (3 bullets)
Title: "Three ways Redwood creates immediate value"
Bullets to say out loud:
1) "Lower unit cost: auto-batching + prefix/KV caching reduce per-token compute by up to ~40% on typical chat workloads (customer benchmark)."
2) "Predictable latency: hardware-aware kernel selection + continuous batching keeps p95 bounded — we provide latency SLAs for Dedicated customers."
3) "Seamless migration path: same API surface across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private so you can start fast and scale safely."
Proof/mini-case: "Fintech customer moved a subset of inference to Dedicated and dropped average 99th percentile latency from 1.8s to 0.6s for chat endpoints while keeping cost per 1k tokens comparable."

Slide 3 — Rapid architecture sketch for a 10–person startup
Title: "3-step rollout for a proof-of-value"
Sketch talking points:
- Step 1: PoC on Hosted API with 1 endpoint + sample prompts (1–2 days)
- Step 2: Dedicated pilot (2–4 weeks) for production traffic and SLA targets; enable autoscaling and burst pools
- Step 3: Optional Private deployment for regulated data (if needed), include KMS/HSM and network controls
Decision triggers: traffic > 1M tokens/month or compliance requirement -> propose Dedicated/Private conversation.

Slide 4 — Objection handling cheatsheet (rapid responses)
Title: "Common customer pushes & quick responses"
Objection: "We need on-prem for data security."
Reply: "We do Private deployments with a customer-managed control plane and HSM/KMS integrations; we can scope an air-gapped package."
Objection: "Costs sound high."
Reply: "We’ll run a workload map and recommend batching/quantization options; many customers see net cost reduction after enabling caching and model selection."
Objection: "We can self-host cheaper."
Reply: "If your focus is serving at scale, most teams underestimate SRE+ops cost. Redwood offloads that and gives predictable unit economics plus fallbacks to keep features live."

Slide 5 — Next-step playbook + assets to leave behind
Title: "Close the loop: what to send after the call"
Immediate follow-ups (pick one):
- Offer a 2-week Hosted trial: include quickstart, sample prompts, and a shared prompt evaluation set
- Offer an architecture session for the platform team (30–45m) to map traffic and SLOs
Sendables:
- One-pager: "Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private at a glance" (attach link)
- Benchmark snippet: p50/p95 numbers for sample workloads
- Cost-estimate template: CSV we populate with customer token volumes

Appendix: Ready-to-use 30s/90s scripts
30s "elevator" script (for SDRs): "We help engineering teams reduce inference latency and unit cost by combining a high-throughput runtime with smart routing and caching. You can start on our Hosted API and move to Dedicated or Private as you scale — preserves the same API and operational tooling."
90s "discovery" script (for AEs): "Teams are struggling with unpredictable latency under burst traffic and rising per-token costs as usage grows. Redwood gives you a unified runtime that picks optimized kernels, applies continuous batching, and routes to lower-cost variants while keeping latency SLOs. The result: better UX for your customers and clearer unit economics for your finance teams — typically customers see a measurable latency improvement and unit-cost savings after a short pilot."

Checklist before sending to customer
- Did I capture persona and their primary SLO? (latency, cost, or compliance)
- Do I have sample prompt that maps to their real workload?
- Which next step am I offering? (trial / arch session / pricing call)

Notes to the field (internal)
- This snackpack is intentionally opinionated: prioritize speed-to-value and a clear migration path.
- Keep numbers conversational; avoid promising exact percentages unless backed by a customer benchmark or recent internal runbook.
- Attach the benchmark CSV for any pricing conversations; route Dedicated/Private asks to solutions-engineering.

Version history
- iter1 2025-08-20: initial draft, compacted slides, added platform hooks
- iter2 2025-09-03: added objection responses and checklist, updated pilot timeline
- iter2 in_review 2025-09-10: added collaborators and linked artifacts for field testing

End of snackpack.
